value: The kelvin (K) is the International System of Units (SI) base unit for thermodynamic temperature, establishing an absolute scale where 0 K represents absolute zero. Developed by Lord Kelvin (William Thomson), its definition has evolved from initial principles based on ideal gas laws and thermodynamic efficiency to the triple point of water, and most recently, in 2019, was redefined in terms of the Boltzmann constant for enhanced precision and independence from specific substances. This fundamental unit is widely applied across various scientific and technical fields, including color temperature measurement, stellar classification in astronomy, and noise temperature in electronics.
